headline: High: open-webui can expose prompts/files to broad-network tools while Prefect can orchestrate downstream actions, creating default-path leakage and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui supports MCP, plugins, OpenAPI tool servers, browsers, and shared web-app sessions, so attacker-controlled content can reach tool-use paths. Prefect is an orchestration system that can consume upstream outputs. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so prompt injection is plausible in default deployments, though not proven from direct interaction evidence.
conditions: IF open-webui ingests untrusted web or document content and forwards it into tool prompts
IF Prefect workflows consume open-webui outputs without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable or restrict MCP/OpenAPI tools in open-webui
Add a provenance tag to all open-webui outputs before Prefect reads them
Require human review for any tool-using prompt chain
Use separate sessions/workspaces for untrusted content
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping filters

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches prompts, chat messages, documents, files, notes, persistent memory, and API keys, and can call cloud APIs and mounted files. Prefect touches workflow metadata and can receive those outputs. If they share a workspace or automation path, sensitive open-webui data can leak into Prefect-managed logs or downstream systems; the profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary.
conditions: IF both agents access the same mounted volume or shared workspace
IF Prefect logs or stores open-webui outputs without redaction
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different volumes
Remove secrets from open-webui prompts and artifacts
Turn off verbose workflow logging in Prefect
Redact files before passing them between agents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent ACLs and secret-scanning

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui has broad network egress, browser/subprocess execution, and shared Redis-backed session state across instances; Prefect is an orchestrator that can also drive networked workflows. Their overlapping write-like influence over shared external resources can conflict if they target the same APIs, files, or workflow state. No locking or coordination is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external API, file, or workflow state
IF no orchestrator-level locking is configured
mitigations: Assign disjoint resource namespaces
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Disable concurrent edits to shared targets
Use idempotent operations where possible
requires-engineering: add distributed locking or transactional updates

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can generate content that Prefect may treat as workflow input, and Prefect is built for orchestration and action-taking. If Prefect executes based on unverified open-webui output, a single hallucination or injected instruction can cascade into automated downstream actions. Because this is a default-path orchestration risk with potentially broad blast radius, high is warranted.
conditions: IF Prefect uses open-webui output as authoritative workflow input
IF no verification or approval step exists before execution
mitigations: Insert a validation step before Prefect runs actions
Require schema checks on all open-webui outputs
Add human approval for destructive workflows
Log and diff proposed actions before execution
requires-engineering: implement policy gates for workflow triggers

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui handles API keys, documents, chat messages, and persistent memory, while Prefect’s documented data class here is workflow metadata. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is visible: if regulated data is routed from open-webui into Prefect logs, retention and subject-rights handling may diverge. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are passed from open-webui into Prefect logs
IF retention settings differ between the two systems
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through Prefect metadata
Shorten log retention on both systems
Mask secrets before orchestration
Document data-flow ownership
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
